title.narrative: Oxfam-Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights Initiative
Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights, initiative

description.narrative:
The Programme aims to contribute to the full exercise of sexual and reproductive health and rights for women, youth, and adolescent girls, mainly indigenous and rural to overcome patriarchal discrimination, exclusion and racism and have the opportunity to dignify their lives by addressing gender based cycles of violence and exercising their rights to health and sexual and reproductive rights.
Specific objcetives:
(i) to defend and promote sexual and reproductive health and rights of girls, women and trans persons in ten regions in Guatemala. (ii) To provide legal assistance, psychosocial care to survivors of violence and sexual violence; this will be achieved through training processes and through working with young male leaders from grass-root organizations.
Försvara och främja SRHR för flickor, kvinnor och transpersoner.

The contribution Promoting Health and Sexual and Reproductive Rights of Maya, Garifuna and Mestizo Adult Women, Young Women, Adolescent Girls and Trans Women in Guatemala, implemented by Oxfam Intermón and eight local partner organizations, during a period of five years. The Swedish contribution to the project is SEK 76,5 million and Oxfam Intermon will contribute with approximately SEK 3,5 million. The objective of this project is to defend and promote the sexual and reproductive health and rights of girls, women and trans persons in 10 regions in Guatemala. Financially, the Swedish funds allocated to this contribution will be used for the carrying out of trainings on sexual and reproductive rights with girls and women; attention and the creation of platforms where organizations of women can meet and discuss common challenges and solutions; the provision of psychosocial care to survivors of sexual violence; to provide legal assistance and accompaniment in cases of sexual violence; and other activities. Additionally, the funds also target young men who have the potential to change the social imaginary and prevent violence against women. This will be achieved through training possesses and through working with young male leaders from grassroot organizations who will, in turn, be able to affect and provide training to other young men. The activities will be implemented by the eight partner organizations and are estimated to benefit a total of more than 62 000 persons, the majority of whom are women. In addition, the project includes advocacy and awareness raising in order to affect institutions and operators working with justice, health and education on SRHR.

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

description.narrative:
The results reported from Oxfam's actions in 2023 include the following:
-Political training processes promoted by the Program, have contributed to increase political women's participation. 16 trained women by the program were registered in the Supreme Electoral Court as electoral observers, during the past electoral process (2023) to elect authorities.
-In order to influence in political candidates in 2023, 11 women's organizations from civil society that are of the SRHR (Sexual and Reproductive, Health and Rights) program, integrated a SRHR political platform. In dialogue with candidates for president and vice president of the Republic, women exposed the existing gaps in the regulatory and institutional frameworks of women's rights, resulting in commitments from these politician to expedite the advancement of legal frameworks.
The results aforementioned are considered relevant due to women in the country face constrainst in exercise their political rights and participate in political decision-making, womens participation in politics is beneficial to both their communities and society in general.
-455 women received sexual and reproductive health care at a community clinic where women have little access to health services. The women received contraceptive methods, free medications and studies to prevent cervical cancer. The program also supported the only clinic in the country that provides difference services and psychological care for women and the LGBTIQ population. 598 people received medical services from professionals who respect sexual orientations and cultural diversity.
-144 women received legal support to denounce physical, sexual and economic violence, these cases are followed up until justice is achieved in the corresponding courts.
-The program promotes awareness processes about SRHR among the population, it also trains women, men, young leaders and midwives to be actors of change (277) in their communities, they replicate the knowledge with other people in their environment. The awareness campaigns in public spaces, social networks and family circles are reached more than 22,464 people.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
